title: I backtested a 10am NQ strategy that wins 6 out of every 10 trades and it still lost $3,675
author: person-person12
selftext:
Win rate used to be the first number i checked on anything i was thinking about running. I stopped doing that after this one.

I ran a popular 10am NQ strategy in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) over july 2023 to feb 2026. 1m candles, 100k account, 1 contract, 535 trades.

* 60.2% win rate
* profit factor 0.98
* net **-$3,675**
* max drawdown 25.55%
* average win $522, average loss $806

It wins **6 out of every 10 trades and still loses money**, because the losers come in about 1.5x the size of the winners. Expected value lands around negative 7 bucks a trade. You can run that for two and a half years, feel right most mornings, and finish the whole thing down.

Its the same as winning six $20 hands and losing four $30 ones. You won more hands than the house did and you still walk out of the casino lighter.

**\_\_\_\_\_\_**

The part that actually changed how i look at a result was the split.

280 of those 535 trades happened in volatile conditions and **those lost $6,764 at a 0.93 profit factor.** The only conditions it made money in were uptrends, 152 trades, 1.08 profit factor, +$3,307. So the thing people are calling an edge is mostly the NASDAQ going up underneath it. Over the same window buy and hold took 100k to roughly 170k.

One blended number across 535 trades hides all of that. The strategy looks flat and slightly unlucky. Split it and its two completely different strategies wearing one name, and the one that fires most often is the one bleeding.

This is also why so many people get a few good months and then watch the thing quietly stop working. Nothing broke, the conditions it was secretly dependent on just ended, and nobody checked which conditions it was holding onto because the summary never said.

**\_\_\_\_\_\_**

The fair part, and this is what id want somebody to say if it was mine getting pulled apart.

What gets taught publicly is the shape, not a rulebook. Mark the 10am candle, wait for a sweep, wait for the move back through, take the continuation. Thats real but its not testable as written, so whoever tests it has to fill in a stop, a cutoff time and a trade limit, and those choices move the result. This run only took longs and entered on a plain break and retest. Both of those are my defaults, not his rules, and either one is worth arguing with.

not advice, a backtest predicts nothing, im just a guy who got tired of reading win rates with no average loss printed next to them. 60.2% of 535 trades were winners and the account still finished $3,675 lighter.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: Average loss next to the win rate should be mandatory tbh. $522 vs $806 says more than the 60% ever did.
